News.title: Should four-day working weeks be banned? Vote now
News.content:
POLL OF THE DAY Should four-day working weeks be banned? Vote now

TORIES have pledged to “end the nonsense” of four-day working weeks if they win the next general election.

A growing movement of firms are promising to offer workers a four-day working week rather than five.





Trials for four-day work weeks were initially launched back in 2022, with 18 UK companies making a permanent change a few months later.

South Cambridgeshire Council is currently the only local authority signed up for a four-day week, but there are thought to be dozens more actively considering the move.

Full-time workers for South Cambridgeshire have a “scheduled rest day” so that their working week is four rather than the traditional five from Monday to Friday.

But James Cleverly has pledged that “the Conservatives will end this nonsense” with a new law to completely ban the practice among public services including councils and schools.

He said: “A four-day working week, where pay is maintained but and hours are reduced, is not value for money and does disservice to hardworking families just trying to get by.”

A total of 254 firms now offer a four day week to their staff.

News.title: Iran releases map for tankers to weave through deadly MINES in Strait of Hormuz – only after they pay $2m ‘Tehran toll’
News.content:
MULLAHS’ MINEFIELD Iran releases map for tankers to weave through deadly MINES in Strait of Hormuz – only after they pay $2m ‘Tehran toll’

IRAN released a chilling map showing how tankers can weave through deadly sea mines dotted throughout the Strait of Hormuz.

It comes after Tehran slapped a $2million (£1.5million) toll on each oil tanker passing through the vital trade route.





Dubbed the ‘Tehran Tollbooth’ each ship must complete a complex and expensive process to be allowed through the strait.

But even then, vessels face a hidden network of Maham 3 and Maham 7 limpet mines which have been poured into the waterway since the start of the conflict.

Any ship crossing can trigger one of the explosives and be blown to pieces.



Iranians released a map to help ship captains navigate the death trap.

The map offers alternative “protected” routes for ships with a clear pathway drawn out with arrows.

A spokesperson for the regime said: “All ships intending to transit the Strait of Hormuz are hereby notified that in order to comply with the principles of maritime safety and to be protected from possible collisions with sea mines, in coordination with the IRGC Navy they should take alternative routes for transiting the Strait of Hormuz.”

Just two oil tankers managed to slip through the Strait after Donald Trump thrashed out a peace deal with Tehran in the 11th hour.



But the rogue nation shut the vital trade route hours later after Iranian Naval officials accused Israel of launching a strike against Lebanon.

A source in the Iranian Navy confirmed the Strait’s closure, telling state media “only Iranian ships and vessels coming from Iran are passing through”.

“Only two oil tankers were able to benefit from the ceasefire and pass through the Strait of Hormuz before ‘Israel’ violated the agreement,” he added.

The ceasefire was contingent on the shipping lane remaining open and is now at risk of collapsing entirely.

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said reports that the Strait was shut were “false”, adding that Trump expects it to be “reopened immediately”.



The White House said Iran‘s original 10-point plan was quickly “thrown in the garbage” by Trump.

He had called the plan “workable” to help facilitate a long-term peace deal but later said the US was sent a different set of agreements by the regime.

The US president has warned the regime to stick to a deal or he will launch a “bigger, and better, and stronger” attack “than anyone has ever seen before”.

Trump said overnight that everything from US warships, aircraft and troops “will remain in place in, and around, Iran, until such time as the REAL AGREEMENT reached is fully complied with.”

It comes after Trump declared the US and Iran could run the Strait of Hormuz as a “beautiful joint venture”.



Meanwhile senior Iranian official insisted that “Iran will punish Israel for its aggression against Lebanon and violations of the ceasefire”.

Iran's version of the 10-point peace plan in full IRAN'S state broadcaster has revealed a ten-point plan which was reportedly sent to the US to help broker a long term peace deal - but the White House said it was "thrown in the garbage". Complete cessation of the war on Iraq, Lebanon, and Yemen Complete and permanent cessation of the war on Iran with no time limit Ending all conflicts in the region in their entirety Reopening the Strait of Hormuz Establishing a protocol and conditions to ensure freedom and security of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz Full payment of compensation for reconstruction costs to Iran Full commitment to lifting sanctions on Iran Release of Iranian funds and frozen assets held by the United States Iran fully commits to not seeking possession of any nuclear weapons Immediate ceasefire takes effect on all fronts immediately upon approval of the above conditions Donald Trump said he is mulling over a 15-point plan to end the war with it unclear what terms are the same as Iran’s and which are different.

At least 112 people were killed and hundreds more wounded in Israel’s latest blitz on the country, their health ministry has claimed.

More than 100 targets were blasted in just ten minutes in the Lebanese capital and the eastern Bekaa valley, its military added.

The US has insisted Lebanon is not part of any ceasefire deal.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Meanwhile Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he “has more goals to complete” in the country.



He added that “the finger is on the trigger” and Israel “is ready to return to fighting at any time” in Iran.

News.title: Moment drunk mum tells van full of kids she drives like a ‘bad b****’ & ‘I’m not responsible if you die’ before crashing
News.content:
THIS is the moment a drunk and high mum told her van full of kids she drives “like a bad b****” before she crashed the vehicle.

The five teenagers can be heard screaming and pleading with Faye Dawson to slow down before she loses control of the van at 80mph.





Sickening footage from the car’s dashcam reveals the 50-year-old mum bragging: “I am a rally car driver and a b****. You get in here with your life.”

Dawson can be seen leaving her home in Staffordshire in the dark before picking up the teens.

She then sped off in the Vauxhall Corsa, asking: “Are you buckled in? Because if you die, I am not responsible for you.”

“I am not a safe driver. Right now I am on alcohol and have had a smoke so I am even more f***ing dangerous,” Dawson adds.



“When it comes to driving, if you are not comfortable do not come in my car.”

Footage shows the reckless mother’s dangerous driving that night – swerving between lanes and cutting across roundabouts before crashing the vehicle at 80mph.

The van careers off the road, hitting the verge and rolling with the passengers trapped inside.

Before the crash, desperate young passengers can be heard instructing one another to “hold on” and repeatedly begging Dawson to “slow down”.



She pleaded guilty to dangerous driving at Stoke-on-Trent Crown Court.

The cruel mother was handed 14 months behind bars and a 55-month driving ban.

The incident occurred in Cheadle, North Staffordshire in March last year.

Judge Richard McConaghy said: “It was a miracle that you did not kill somebody.”

The court heard how four of the five children were injured in the horror smash after Dawson lost control of the van.



The injured teens were aged between 14 and 15 years old and one suffered a spine fracture in the crash.

This girl told the court of her terror during the car ride and the ongoing impact of her injury.

“I thought I was going to die,” she said. “I had to have time off school to recover.”

“I feel very anxious in vehicles. I have nightmares and flashbacks. I had to live with back pain for six months.”

Another of the teenagers had a statement read out in court which told of their trauma from the petrifying journey.



They recalled: “I felt trapped and terrified. I felt powerless. I remember screaming.

“I genuinely believed I was going to die. I have suffered flashbacks and panic attacks. I was shaking uncontrollably.”

Judge McConaghy made a scorching assessment of Dawson’s culpability in his sentencing remarks.

He told the disgraced mother: “Your appalling arrogance caught up with you. When doing nearly 80mph you lost control of the car and rolled it.

“You injured a number of your passengers. It was a miracle that you did not kill somebody.



“You were recorded shouting about what had happened to your car, not about what had happened to the children who were in it.

“You are lucky that you have been charged with dangerous driving and not causing serious injury by dangerous driving.

“You made a deliberate decision to ignore the rules of the road. Your driving was impaired by the consumption of alcohol and drugs.”

The judge added he was not convinced Dawson showed any real remorse for the crash and the impact it has had on the young passengers.

Her defence barrister, Robert Holt, said Dawson had withdrawn from the world and had PTSD from the horrific crash.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“She will never drive again, such is the traumatic effect of what took place,” he said.

“She feels genuine remorse and empathy with the people in the car that night. She has no interest in driving again.”

News.title: Four people die after small boat sinks crossing Channel – as France rejects UK’s offer to intercept and return migrants
News.content:
FOUR people have died after a small-boat sank while crossing the Channel as France rejects the UK’s offer to intercept and return migrants.

Two men and two women died off the coast of northern France after being swept away by strong currents trying to board a dinghy.





At least 42 others were rescued in the incident off the coast of Boulogne, between Equihen-Plage and Hardelot-Plage.

Francois-Xavier Lauch, the prefect of Pas-de-Calais, told reporters on Thursday: “We sadly have to report four deaths this morning.

“The people who died were attempting to board a taxi-boat.

“I have to commend the actions of our officers and firefighters who, as you know, are deployed every day to stop these crossings.”

Speaking of the four people who died, he said: “They were already quite far into the sea.

“The currents, which can be dangerous here, swept them away.

“This provisional toll – and I insist that it is provisional – states four deceased: two men, two women.”

One person also suffered hypothermia, and another 37 other people are currently being treated by emergency services.



A number of other small boats are currently at sea and being monitored by French authorities, including a military helicopter, Mr Lauch added.

In the first two months of 2026, around 2,200 migrants crossed the Channel to the UK with about 41,500 crossing last year.

On Tuesday, 137 arrived from France aboard two makeshift inflatables, bringing the total number this year to more than 5000.

And yesterday, 102 migrants were rescued after getting into trouble during an attempt to cross the Channel.

It comes as a plan to allow British boats to intercept migrants at sea and return them to France has been firmly rejected by President Emmanuel Macron’s government.



Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood wanted to deploy her department’s Border Force fleet in a “more active role” in the English Channel to bring down the number of asylum seekers reaching England.

Ms Mahmood suggested the Border Force interception option as part of negotiations to renew a multimillion-pound migrant patrol deal during an impasse in talks between London and Paris.

It would have seen up to 11 British vessels, including six 42-metre Border Force cutters, bolstering French patrols at sea.

The British would have intercepted small boats before they reached UK waters, picked up the migrants on board, and taken them back to northern France.



But a government source in Paris said: “The idea was firmly rejected because British government officials are not meant to operate in French territorial waters.”

Details of the proposed plan were revealed by French investigative newspaper, Le Canard Enchaîné.

Its latest edition revealed how British taxpayers funded 100 new police vehicles currently used to look for migrants and smugglers.

This amounts to 25% of the total number of police vehicles France deploys in the north of the country, around Calais and Dunkirk.

France and Britain have agreed a temporary two-month extension to the current deal that pays for French police to patrol beaches for migrants after negotiations failed to agree on new terms.



The UK will pay the French £16.5 million to cover the cost of nearly 700 police officers patrolling northern France until May.

This is the equivalent of £275,000 per day, or £2million a week.

The extension was officially designed to prevent a surge in migrant crossings during the current spell of good weather.

Negotiations to agree a new three-year deal are also deadlocked over Ms Mahmood’s demands for the French to deploy more officers on beaches.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She also wants strict payment-by-results conditions, but the French are fiercely opposed to this too.



The Home Office confirmed most of the details in the Canard Enchaîné article, but denied that Britain was billed almost £20 million by France’s Republican Security Companies riot squad to buy a new helicopter.

News.title: Brits say goodbye to 26C scorcher as temps set to plunge to 4C in parts of UK with heavy rain and cooler weather TODAY
News.content:
BRITS soaked up a sizzling 26C scorcher on one of the hottest early April days ever – before being warned to brace for a dramatic drop to just 5C.

Forecasters said yesterday was the hottest day of the year so far and the warmest April day recorded since 1946.





Sun seekers flocked to parks and beer gardens as temperatures soared to 26.6C in Kew Gardens, south west London.

Parts of the UK were even hotter than holiday hotspots like Ibiza, Rome and Marrakech.

But the Met Office flagged a “big change” today, with the warm spell set to come to an abrupt end.

Meteorologist Tom Morgan said the spike in temperatures was “uncommon” before warning of the drop today.

He said: “Temperatures even into the mid 20s are very uncommon at this time of year.

“In the London area, we’ve seen temperatures above 26C, and currently the provisional maximum today is 26.6C in Kew Gardens, London.



“And that is pretty exceptional for at least the first half of April.

“It’s been very, very warm, but it is a brief peak in the heat, with temperatures for most of the UK considerably lower tomorrow.”

Another forecaster said the taste of summer will be “short-lived”.

Met Office Chief Forecaster Paul Gundersen warned: “We’re seeing a brief but notable spell of very warm weather for early April, with temperatures more typically associated with late spring or early summer.

“This could be the warmest spell at this point in April since 2020.



“However, this warmth will be short-lived, with a marked drop in temperatures and more unsettled conditions developing later this week.

“In some areas, daytime temperatures could fall by around 10°C between Wednesday and Thursday.”

From today, cooler air will sweep in from the northwest, bringing a sharp change in conditions.

While parts of the southeast and East Anglia may cling on to some warmth, much of the country will see temperatures fall.

Brits are warned of showers spreading and winds picking up in strength.



By tonight, it will feel a world away from the balmy evenings earlier this week, with a risk of frost in some areas.

And things only get worse heading into the weekend.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Brits can expect blustery winds, frequent showers and far more typical spring temperatures.

The forecast for Friday, Saturday and Sunday looks unsettled throughout, with further bands of rain and showers.

News.title: Shock arrest after US woman fell overboard from dinghy on Bahamas holiday with husband – as her daughter breaks silence
News.content:
POLICE PROBE Shock arrest after US woman fell overboard from dinghy on Bahamas holiday with husband – as her daughter breaks silence

THE husband of a woman who disappeared off a boat has been arrested, according to reports.

Lynette Hooker, 55, vanished from the eight-foot hard-bottom dinghy and was reportedly swept away by the currents.





A 59-year-old man has now reportedly been arrested by local police on Wednesday evening in connection with Lynette’s disappearance.

Her husband, Brian Hooker, 59, is reportedly the person arrested.

No charges have been confirmed.

Lynette allegedly fell into the sea from the dinghy when the pair was trying to reach their yacht, Soulmate, reported The New York Post.

She was said to be carrying the boat’s keys, causing the vessel’s engine to shut down, said police.

Hooker claimed he lost sight of her and paddled back to shore, arriving at around 4am on Sunday. The incident was then reported to police.

But her daughter, Karli Aylesworth, said she believes “something might have happened” involving her mom and stepdad.



“I do believe something might have happened to her,” she said to Fox News.

“There’s history of him choking her out and threatening to throw her overboard.

“So the fact that this is actually happening makes me believe there’s more to the story.”

Aylesworth also claimed that her stepdad did not tell her that her mom, who is 55, was missing until 24 hours after her disappearance.

Hooker denied the claims.



“I categorically deny the allegations made by Karli Aylesworth,” he told The Daily Beast.

“At this time, I have retained local counsel, Terrel Butler, and I am acting on her strict advice not to provide further comment to the press, as there is currently an ongoing investigation.”

However, he also took to Facebook to describe his heartbreak.



“I am heartbroken over the recent boat accident in unpredictable seas and high winds that caused my beloved Lynette to fall from our small dinghy near Elbow Cay in the Bahamas,” he wrote.



“Despite desperate attempts to reach her, the winds and currents drove us further apart. We continue to search for her, and that is my sole focus.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The pair from Onsted, Michigan, has been married for more than 20 years.

Authorities continue to conduct searches for Lynette.

News.title: Body found in grounds of castle by cops hunting for lad, 17, who vanished from popular beauty spot
News.content:
TRAGIC DISCOVERY Body found in grounds of castle by cops hunting for lad, 17, who vanished from popular beauty spot

A BODY has been found in the search for a missing teenager who entered a lake in the grounds of a castle.

Emergency crews scrambled to Chirk Castle in Wrexham, North Wales, after a 17-year-old entered the water on Tuesday.



After two days of searching by specialist teams, a body has tragically been found at the castle, which is next to a National Trust site.



The death is not being treated as suspicious.

Formal identification has yet to take place, but the family of the 17-year-old have been informed.

Detective Chief Superintendent Sian Beck said: “My deepest thoughts and condolences are with his loved ones, who are being supported by specialist officers following this tragic incident.

“Formal identification is yet to take place, but his family have been informed.

“We kindly ask that the privacy of the family is respected at this difficult time.”

A spokesperson for the force said previously: “Emergency Services are currently responding to an incident at Chirk Castle.

“A 17-year-old male is believed to have entered water within the castle’s grounds yesterday afternoon and has not been seen since.

“Specialist search and rescue teams are continuing their efforts to locate the missing teenager.”



A spokesperson for National Trust Cymru confirmed crews were accessing the water through the trust’s grounds on Tuesday.

They said: “We are aware of an ongoing incident on land neighbouring National Trust Cymru’s estate at Chirk Castle.

“The emergency services are in attendance, with access provided via our estate. All enquiries should be directed to North Wales Police.”

West Midlands Ambulance Service were in attendance, alongside crews from the Welsh Ambulance Service (WAS).

A WAS spokesperson said: “We were called at around 4pm yesterday (Tuesday) to an incident at Chirk Castle, Wrexham.



“We sent one emergency ambulance to the scene, where the crew was supported by one Cymru High Acuity Response Unit and two operations managers.

“Emergency Medical Retrieval and Transfer Service colleagues also attended in a Wales Air Ambulance charity helicopter.”

News.title: British mum, 47, and daughter, 19, caught ‘trying to smuggle 42kg of cocaine in their luggage’ at Spanish airport
News.content:
DRUG ARREST British mum, 47, and daughter, 19, caught ‘trying to smuggle 42kg of cocaine in their luggage’ at Spanish airport

A BRIT mum and her teen daughter have been arrested at a Spanish airport after police allegedly found 42kg of cocaine in their luggage.

The pair, aged 47 and 19, are accused of posing as tourists visiting Valencia over Easter before attempting to fly home with the drugs.





They were caught last Thursday at around 11pm as they prepared to jet off back to Birmingham from Valencia’s Manises Airport.

Around 23 sealed packets of cocaine and multiple tablets were found stuffed inside two suitcases, according to local media.

Both had arrived in the beaming sun of Valencia just three days earlier.

They were remanded to a local jail after appearing before a judge in Quart de Poblet, a municipality near Valencia.



Police are yet to make any official comment on the result of the trial or if the pair have been charged.

It comes after ex-Premier League ace Neil Clement was identified as the man arrested by police on the Costa del Sol during a dramatic drugs raid.

The 47-year-old ex-West Brom and Chelsea defender was hauled into custody by undercover cops during the major narcotics bust.

Clement was held at an allegedly illegal weed club called Doobiez after undercover cops intercepted a punter who claimed he had just acquired his bag of cannabis there.



Police seized more drugs and cash inside the premises before marching the retired defender, son of former QPR and England legend Dave Clement, out in handcuffs.

The dad-of-two ex-England U16 and U18 player, whose older brother Paul is Brazil’s current assistant coach, appeared in court where a judge released him on bail pending investigations.

Last May, a Brit couple claiming to be tourists from Thailand were caught with more than 33kg of cannabis in their suitcases at Valencia’s airport.

The pair were picked out by suspicious cops after displaying a “nervous and evasive attitude”.

The man and woman, aged 33 and 34, were stopped before reaching customs, with officials later discovering vacuum-packed marijuana and no clothes or personal belongings in their luggage.

News.title: Prince Harry's desperate plea to King Charles before he married Queen Camilla
News.content:
Prince Harry's desperate plea to King Charles before he married Queen Camilla

It's been 21 years to the day since the King and Queen tied the knot, but before their low-key nuptials, Harry pleaded with his father to not marry Camilla for one major reason

View 4 Images Harry and Camilla had a strained relationship in the early days of her relationship with Charles (Image: WireImage)

It's been 21 years to the day since King Charles and Queen Camilla finally said their vows in what was a second wedding for both of them.

‌



Charles had previously been wedded to Princess Diana, with the couple divorcing just a year prior to her tragic death at the age of 36 in 1997. Camilla had also been married before to her first husband Andrew Parker Bowles, with whom she shares two children. When Charles and Camilla's big day arrived on April 9 2005, both Princes William and Harry were present to witness their father remarry, as were Camilla's two children, Tom and Laura.

‌



View 4 Images King Charles and Queen Camilla are celebrating their 21st wedding anniversary today (Image: Corbis via Getty Images)

‌



However, it appears that Harry once implored his father not to marry Camilla. In his controversial memoir Spare, Harry recounts how he and William perceived Camilla as having played a "pivotal role in the unravelling of our parents' marriage" but simultaneously recognised how she brought happiness to their father.

He notes that when asked, he and William assured their dad that they'd accept Camilla into the family. Nonetheless, he added: "The only thing we asked in return was that he not marry her. You don't need to remarry, we pleaded.

"A wedding would cause controversy. It would incite the press. It would make the whole country, the whole world, talk about Mummy, compare Mummy and Camilla, and nobody wanted that. Least of all Camilla."

‌



View 4 Images Harry reportedly pleaded with Charles to not marry Camilla (Image: Getty Images)

Although Charles and Camilla made their relationship public in the early 2000s - some years following Princess Diana's death - his sons weren't photographed with her publicly until 12 months later. When Harry first met Camilla as a teenager, their meeting was reportedly uncomfortable and strained. He was merely 13, desperately missing his mother.

In the book Prince William: Born to be King, a palace insider reveals to royal biographer Penny Junor: "I think the relationship between them all is warm now but if I'm honest, it wasn't then. I think they found it hard. To be fair to Camilla, she never tried to be mummy but she was the 'other woman' and she was there and taking daddy's time."

‌



Meanwhile, in The Palace Papers by royal writer and former Vanity Fair editor Tina Brown, she claims that Harry "unnerved Camilla". According to The Telegraph, the book quotes a courtier as saying: "When the younger boy was eventually prevailed upon to be in the presence of Mrs Parker Bowles, he unnerved her with long silences and smouldering, resentful stares."

View 4 Images The relationship between Harry and Camilla reportedly improved over time (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

As the years passed, Harry and William did seem to forge a closer bond with Camilla. During a conversation marking his 21st birthday in 2005, Harry stated that he and his brother "loved her to bits" and he also openly acknowledged her for making their father "very, very happy".

However, a friend of the princes revealed: "Although tensions have eased between the two of them over the years, it was more for a show of unity than a close relationship. There were big problems at the start but as Harry and his brother William aged and matured, things got better and they can now co-exist as adults. They were never close with her and they still aren't."

News.title: Town with its own post office and hotel on sale for price of one-bed flat
News.content:
Town with its own post office and hotel on sale for price of one-bed flat

A town in Australia's outback has gone up for sale at an astonishingly low price comes with its own motel, post office, and pub that attracts people from miles around

View 3 Images A town of just two is up for sale (Image: Shutterstock)

An entire town with a population of just two people is up for sale as the inhabitants of the town of have decided to leave.

‌



Lying deep in the heart of Australian state Queensland’s outback sits Cooladdi, whose name apparently stems form the Indigenous word for ‘black duck’, used to be a busy railway hub and once had a population of up to 270 people.

‌



According to reports, the town’s population began to shrink because the local sheep industry declined and trains stopped coming to the area, leading to the dramatic population shrinkage.

‌



The area, 500 miles from the city of Brisbane, is now up for sale for just $400,000 (£209,920). And with that, they will get the Foxtrap Roadhouse, the keys to the town and a four-bedroom house.

For perspective, £200k may only be enough to nab you a one-bedroom flat outside London in the UK.

Meanwhile in Australia, the nearest major town to Cooladdi, the 3,000 strong Charleville, has an average house price of around $210,000 (£110,208). The price to buy the town is a far cry from the average price of a flat in Sydney that currently sits at around $935,000 (£490,688).

‌



View 3 Images The town of Cooladdi is up for sale (Image: Getty)

Although Cooladdi is undoubtedly a small town, it has its own post office and its own postcode of 4479.

‌



Cooladdi’s current inhabitants, Jo Cornel and Carol Yarrow, have lived in Cooladdi since February 2023, but have now decided to return to Brisbane as Jo wants to be closer to family and Carol is coming up on retirement.

Speaking to ABC about the matter, Carol said: “I've just turned 70 and finding I'm getting a bit old for it. Let's hope somebody else can get in and do the same thing.”

View 3 Images Cooladdi has just two residents (Image: Getty)

‌



Although the pair are miles from the nearest people, they say there is still a bustling community of people who travel around 70km (43.496 miles) to Cooladdi.

Carol told the Guardian: “The food and the pub are probably one of the main jobs; we also do the mail runs as part of the post office.

“I’ve always found the best thing is the local community … the people within around 70km who come through the property.”

Article continues below

The sale of Cooladdi is currently being managed by local estate agents Charleville Real Estate and Becky Jeisman who highlighted how the town, though small, would offer a “great change of pace” for those who chose to buy it and that, if four people bought it, the population would double.

News.title: Police in the Bahamas arrest husband of US woman who vanished from boat
News.content:
Police in the Bahamas arrest husband of US woman who vanished from boat

Lynette Hooker vanished while on a sailing holiday with her husband in the Caribbean, he told cops she fell overboard - now police have arrested a man, 59, who is being questioned

View 4 Images Missing American woman Lynette Hooker and her husband Brian Hooker (Image: @ the_sailing_hookers / Instagram)

The husband of a woman who vanished while sailing on a holiday in the Bahamas has been arrested.

‌



Lynette Hooker, 55, was reported missing on Saturday night after she plunged into the water on a boating trip in the holiday hotspot. Officials said the American woman was travelling in an 8-foot motorboat from Hope Town to Elbow Cay, and that her husband, Brian Hooker, told authorities she fell overboard with the boat keys, causing the engine to turn off.

‌



Authorities on the Caribbean island said the 59-year-old man, who they did not identify, was detained in Abaco and is being questioned by the Royal Bahamas Police Force.

‌



View 4 Images The 55-year-old vanished while on a boat in the Bahamas (Image: Facebook)

Missing girl found after 32 year search was working for private investigator when found READ MORE :

Last moments of woman walking in dark boatyard before vanishing 4 weeks ago READ MORE :

This shocking update came after the couple's daughter called for a full investigation into her mum's death, adding that "prior issues" have come to her attention. A Coast Guard spokesperson said late on Wednesday that they have opened a criminal investigation into the case.

Cops did not share further details, including whether the husband has been charged or not. Authorities added that the husband had paddled back to shore after his wife fell into the water and told someone about her disappearance early on Sunday.

‌



View 4 Images Lynette's husband was arrested in the Bahamas (Image: Facebook)

Police in the Bahamas said: "Strong currents subsequently carried her away, and he lost sight of her." Lynette Hooker's mum, Darlene Hamlett, said on Wednesday that she was "glad to hear" about the arrest, but declined further comment, saying she was seeking more information.

Earlier on Wednesday, the mum said she wanted to hear more from Brian Hooker about what happened to her daughter on holiday. Ms Hamlett had said: "I'm going to be interested in what he says, because I haven't heard from him in almost two days.

‌



"Our family grew up on water and so Lynette her whole life has been near lakes, on boats, sailing and swimming. It would be a miracle if (she's rescued), but I'm still counting on one." Lynette and Brian had been married for more than two decades and lived in Onsted, Michigan.

View 4 Images Karli Aylesworth said it was unlikely that her mum would "just fall" off a boat (Image: NBC News)

Lynette Hooker's daughter, Karli Aylesworth, speaking to NBC News, said it was not likely that her mum would "just fall" off a boat because the 55-year-old was an experienced sailor.

Article continues below

The daughter added that her parents' relationship was not consistent and they had a "history of not getting along, especially when they drink". Aylesworth added that she didn't think her mum was able to tread water for that long and thought she wouldn't have survived, but hoped to find her for closure.

On Wednesday morning, Brian Hooker, on Facebook, said that he is "heartbroken over the recent boat accident in unpredictable seas and high winds that caused my beloved Lynette to fall from our small dinghy near Elbow Cay in the Bahamas".

The husband added: "Despite desperate attempts to reach her, the winds and currents drove us further apart. We continue to search for her and that is my sole focus." Bahamian police said search operations and investigative efforts remain active.

News.title: 'My dog and I both had breast cancer and went through same treatment'
News.content:
'My dog and I both had breast cancer and went through same treatment'

Vickie Doogan got Dolly to help her during her recovery, but things turned out differently

View 3 Images Vickie Doogan with her dog Dolly (Image: Vickie Doogan/SWNS)

A woman who got a dog to help her through a second breast cancer diagnosis was shocked when her pooch was struck by the same disease and also needed a mastectomy. Vickie Doogan, 52, was first diagnosed with breast cancer aged 39, after discovering a lump in her left arm.

‌



Vickie was shocked, as she was fit and healthy, but thankfully responded to chemotherapy well and bounced back after her treatment. However, when she was 44 she was diagnosed again and went through a double mastectomy to lower the chances of the cancer returning for a third time.

‌



She got Dolly, a Poochon, to support her during her recovery, but seven years later, in February 2026, the roles were reversed when Dolly was also diagnosed with breast cancer, after Vickie took her to the vets as she had stomach pain. The pooch had to go through a doggy mastectomy, but thankfully bounced back as quickly as her owner. The pair are now both cancer-free and Vickie is keen to show that you can live a full life, despite a cancer diagnosis.

‌



Vickie, a recruiter from Ascot, Berkshire, said: "When I was first diagnosed with breast cancer, I was absolutely floored. I was 39, fit, healthy, and there was no lump in my breast.

"Chemo was brutal, but thankfully I responded well to it. In 2018, when I was diagnosed again, I just couldn't believe it.

"I found out I have the altered BRCA2 gene, meaning I'm more predisposed to breast cancer, so I had an elective double mastectomy. The surgery was amazing; I had implants put in the next day.

‌



"I got Dolly after my second diagnosis to be my buddy, as I was at home a lot. She's like my shadow, she's the most perfect little dog.

View 3 Images Vickie Doogan, 52, was first diagnosed with breast cancer in 2013 (Image: Vickie Doogan/SWNS)

"In February 2026, I took Dolly to the vet as she had an upset stomach and they found a lump under one of her nipples. The vet said she needed to have a mastectomy, I was so shocked, I didn't even know dogs could have mastectomies.

‌



"She bounced back just as well as I did, people said it's like she's mirroring how I dealt with it. Now I'm living my best life again, it's all in my past. I want people to know that although breast cancer is scary, you can still live a really full life."

Vickie first realised something wasn't right in November 2013, as she noticed a dull pain under her arm. "I was the fittest and healthiest I'd ever been and I was really looking forward to turning 40," she said.

At first, she thought the pain could be due to swollen glands under her arm, but after feeling a lump her intuition told her it was something more. She went to her GP, who referred her to a Breast Care Unit, where she had a biopsy that showed she had invasive breast cancer, which had migrated to her arm.

‌



The diagnosis shocked and angered Vickie, as she was fit and healthy and there hadn't been a lump on her breast. She was immediately put on eight rounds of "brutal" chemotherapy, which she thankfully responded well to, and then had a lumpectomy to remove the remaining cancer.

After 15 rounds of radiotherapy and a year and a half of taking monthly oestrogen blockers, Vickie was delighted to be cancer-free. She began embracing life again, but following her fifth annual mammogram in 2018, she was shocked to discover that the cancer had returned.

Doctors were shocked that the cancer had returned, due to her age, and she underwent genetic testing, where it was discovered that she has the altered BRCA2 gene, meaning she is more predisposed to breast cancer. "It made perfect sense to me; I was glad to have some reasoning behind it," Vickie said.

‌



She went back for more chemotherapy and, due to the genetic mutation, Vickie had an elective double mastectomy to lower the risk of the cancer returning. The surgery went well and Vickie was able to have reconstruction on the same day.

View 3 Images Vickie Doogan was shocked, as she was fit and healthy (Image: Vickie Doogan/SWNS)

During her recovery, Vickie decided to get a dog to help her feel calmer and more comfortable while she was at home. She brought Poochon Dolly home with her in October 2018.

‌



She immediately fell in love with the pooch, but in February 2026, she noticed that Dolly had an upset stomach. She took her to the vet, who examined her and found a lump under one of her nipples.

Dolly had to have a "doggy mastectomy" to remove the cancer and, fortunately, as it was low grade, didn't need any follow-up treatment. The duo are now both cancer-free.

Vickie is one of the people affected by breast cancer in Breast Cancer Now's new television advert. She is supporting charity Breast Cancer Now, as new figures reveal that there are almost one million people (920,000) people living with or beyond a diagnosis of breast cancer in the UK, a figure projected to rise to more than 1.4 million by 2050.

Article continues below

The charity has committed to be 'Breast Cancer Now until we're Breast Cancer Never' - in line with its bold ambition that by 2050, everyone with breast cancer will live and live well. Breast Cancer Now's objective it to keep going until there is a future where everyone with breast cancer lives and lives well. Find out more at breastcancernow.org

News.title: Four people die attempting to cross English Channel in small boat
News.content:
Four people die attempting to cross English Channel in small boat

Four people, two men and two women, have died after trying to cross the English Channel in a small boat - we'll be bringing you the very latest updates, pictures and video on this breaking news story.

View Image Migrants prepare to board a dinghy before attempting to sail into the English Channel on April 1, 2026 in Gravelines, France (Image: Tom Nicholson/Getty)

Two men and two women have died after attempting to cross the English Channel in a small boat.

‌



The head of the Pas-de-Calais region, Francois-Xavier Lauch, said the four migrants were "far out to sea" when their bodies were found by authorities. Another 42 were rescued and brought to shore in France.

‌



“We sadly have to report four deaths this morning,” Mr Lauch told reporters this morning, adding they were attempting to board a “taxi-boat” – another term for dinghy – near the seaside town of Equihen-Plage.

‌



“I have to commend the actions of our officers and firefighters who, as you know, are deployed every day to stop these crossings,” the prefect said.

Speaking of the four people who died, he said: “They were already quite far into the sea.

“The currents, which can be dangerous here, swept them away.

‌



“This provisional toll – and I insist that it is provisional – states four deceased: two men, two women,”

One person also suffered hypothermia, and another 37 other people are currently being treated by emergency services.

A number of dinghies are currently at sea and being monitored by the French authorities, including a military helicopter, Mr Lauch added.

‌



“The responsibility lies with the smugglers,” he told reporters.

A government spokesperson said: “We are deeply saddened to hear about the deaths in French waters today.

“Every death in the Channel is a tragedy and a stark reminder of the dangers posed by criminal gangs exploiting vulnerable people for profit. We will continue working relentlessly with the French and our partners overseas to prevent these perilous journeys.

‌



“The French authorities are leading the response to this incident and we are supporting their investigation.”

It comes after two migrants died crossing the English Channel in a separate incident last week, with six rescued and one of them rushed to hospital for further care.

In another incident, two women and a man were burnt when their small boat caught fire off the coast at Le Portel, local media reported.

‌



A 17-year-old woman suffered burns all over her body and 77 people had to be rescued.

Over 300 people are estimated to have crossed the Channel yesterday as Britain experienced the warmest day of the year so far.

But the number of migrants who have arrived in the UK in small boats in the first three months of 2026 was down by a third compared with the same period last year, Home Office figures show.

News.title: Families living near chemical plant told to stop eating home-grown veg over contamination fears
News.content:
Families living near chemical plant told to stop eating home-grown veg over contamination fears

Hundreds of households near a former chemical plant have been warned due to contamination fears

Families' 'toxic soil' fears living near chemical plant

Families living near a former chemical plant have been advised not to eat vegetables grown in their gardens or eggs laid by pet chickens amid concerns they contain cancer-causing toxins. Hundreds of households within a one-kilometre radius of the former ICI plant at Thornton-Cleveleys, Lancashire, have been warned their gardens could be contaminated with deadly 'forever chemicals'.

‌



Tests have revealed that Perfluorooctanoic Acid (PFOA) - a chemical commonly used to coat non-stick pans - has been discovered in the soil of 71 properties surrounding the plant. However, it is believed that approximately 250 properties are at 'high risk', according to Wyre Council Leader Michael Vincent.

‌



PFOA is known to accumulate in the blood and can trigger cancer, immune system disorders, as well as dangerously high cholesterol levels. A group of around 60 residents are now considering pursuing legal action over the contamination with the assistance of environmental law firm Leigh Day.

‌



One local resident has spoken out about how she suffered a sudden and unexplained stroke, having consumed eggs, fruit and vegetables from her garden for more than a decade. Mother-of-four Sam Linacre-Hammond, 48, regularly grew produce including potatoes, tomatoes and strawberries, and also kept hens and ducks whose eggs her family consumed.

View 6 Images Sam says that some of her ducks have died suddenly (Image: SWNS)

Samantha suffered a cryptogenic - or unexplained - stroke in 2020, which she attributes to the consumption of contaminated food. The mother of four said: "It makes me angry and guilty for poisoning my children for all of these years.

‌



"We would eat two eggs a day each, which we would have in sandwiches or use while baking and the veggies were used in most dinners. I used the area a lot with my children, now it is abandoned, we don't dare go on it anymore." I was fit, healthy, and a low risk for something like this to happen, reports Lancs Live.

"The only thing doctors said that could have caused it was high cholesterol. I have never suffered from high cholesterol ever and now I'm on two medications to keep it down. There are a lot of unanswered questions but I think it is the poison."

Sam purchased an eighth-of-an-acre plot of land adjacent to her home - situated roughly 400 metres from the former Thornton ICI plant - from Wyre Council in 2011. Last month, Wyre Council confirmed that scientists had tested eggs from a small number of domestic poultry keepers within 0.6 miles (1km) of the former ICI site.

‌



View 6 Images The former ICI site, now operated by AGC Chemicals Europe Ltd, within the Hillhouse Technology Enterprise Zone in Thornton-Cleveleys (Image: SWNS)

The Food Standards Agency informed Sam that consuming just one of her duck eggs would exceed the safe weekly limit - though she disclosed she had stopped eating them a year earlier upon receiving her first warning. The neighbouring allotment beside her plot on Occupation Road has since been shut down by the council after meeting the statutory criteria for formal classification as "Contaminated Land", with any consumption of produce grown there posing a potential "harm to health ".

The Food Standards Agency stated this is due to the fact that people who consume "large quantities of vegetables on a daily basis from Occupation Road Allotments are likely to be increasing their exposure to PFAS (Per- and Poly-Fluorinated Substances)". A multi-agency probe, involving the council and the Environment Agency (EA), into the contamination by PFOA from the ICI site was launched in 2024.

‌



PFOA belongs to the same chemical family as PFAS, commonly referred to as "forever chemicals". According to charity CHEM Trust, virtually everybody carries chemicals from the PFAS family in their body. Nevertheless, elevated levels pose grave risks to health.

BBC Morning Live Dr Xand gives 'hottest' clothes tip to keep Norovirus away READ MORE :

The investigation followed the EA obtaining information suggesting historic emissions of PFOA from the ICI site, now operating as AGC Chemicals Europe Ltd. It is thought the ICI factory had been releasing PFOA into the atmosphere from the 1950s, right up until 2012 when it was phased out.

At the time, the substance complied with UK legislation - however it was subsequently classified as a carcinogen, meaning it causes cancer. In 2024, the council dispatched letters to local residents warning them not to consume anything grown in their plots. While early advice given was to wash and peel any home-grown produce to remove potentially contaminated soil or dust, three phases of soil testing have since been carried out to establish the level of risk. Last year it emerged that all allotment soil samples near the site recorded detectable PFOA concentrations, with a maximum of 20.2μg/kg and an average of 5.92μg/kg.

‌



This significantly surpasses the precautionary screening value of 1.4μg/kg by nearly five times. Additional samples were subsequently taken from 63 locations within 500m of the AGC facility, including private gardens.

Of the 291 soil samples collected, 287 (99%) showed elevated PFOA with a maximum value of 144μg/kg (average 4.18μg/kg), compared to a screening threshold of 7.6ug/kg for gardens where vegetables are cultivated.

View 6 Images The precautionary advice is linked to an investigation into historic contamination from part of the former ICI site (Image: SWNS)

‌



The summary notes that "The results paint a picture of sporadic contamination, indicating zones of 'higher' and 'lower' risk". To date, soil samples from 71 properties have revealed the presence of PFOA near the site, though some affected properties have been constructed on parts of the former ICI location.

While no action was considered necessary in the vast majority of cases, seven "high risk" properties require further investigation, one of which belonged to Sam. Wyre Council Leader Michael Vincent says residents have a 'right to be upset'.

"I feel their frustration, and residents need answers," he said. "I don't have an exact number of properties to hand for the 1km zone, but there are around 1,000 in total.

‌



"The higher risk area is to the South / South West of the site. I'd say it was no more than 250 in the high-risk area. We have test results back from 71 properties within the 1km zone as part of phase 3. Of those, 7 are considered higher risk and need further investigation. The other 64 will not need any further investigation but the 7 will.

"The EA and partner agencies are currently planning phase 4 and the council want to be sure it's done in a way that means every household in the gets a safe, reliable answer regarding contaminated land. We are committed, and our focus is to get this resolved urgently so the cleanup can begin. Our investigation is separate from any health-related inquiries, something I know residents are also worried about.

"I understand there has been talk of legal action, and my advice is that residents should be taking correct legal advice if there is a genuine claim."

‌



View 6 Images Sam Hammond rears ducks and grows fruit and herbs in her large garden, directly next door to the allotment on Hargate Road which has been contaminated with chemicals (Image: SWNS)

Cllr Vincent offered no indication of when any clean-up work might get under way. Retired couple Frank, 80, and Marlowe Howarth, 72, who reside over a mile south of the plant on Rosendale Avenue, said it 'wasn't nice' to receive the letters, but they don't believe it has had any impact on them. It follows news that an allotment on a nearby street, Sandringham Avenue, has also been shut by the council as a precautionary measure after the findings from Occupation Road. Frank said: "We live a distance away, but it hasn't been nice to receive those letters in the post, especially the thought of knowing it may have spread this far.

"We think the council were just being cautious about sharing the letters with us, we still eat apples from the neighbour's garden in the summer."

‌



View 6 Images Marlowe and Frank Howarth said it 'hasn't been nice to receive those letters' warning them of the potential health implications (Image: SWNS)

According to Wyre Council, no other parcels of land besides Occupation Road, whether publicly or privately owned, have been designated as contaminated under Part 2A of the Environmental Protection Act 1990.

This is the legislation that creates a legal framework for addressing contaminated land in England, according to the government. Wyre Council has repeatedly stated it is supporting residents impacted by the pollution.

‌



A spokesperson for AGC Chemicals Europe said they have since launched their own voluntary on-site investigation into the contamination, and it is their 'highest priority' to support the affected community. The EA say they are backing the multi-agency response.

View 6 Images An investigation into the former ICI site regarding historic contamination has been launched (Image: SWNS)

A spokesperson for the multi-agency group conducting the investigation said: "The investigation has now reached a challenging stage where we have gathered important data, but this information must undergo thorough scientific interpretation before we can answer the questions we know the community will have.

Article continues below

"Throughout this process, we have made transparency with the community our priority and we will continue to share updates as soon as we receive further information."

Leigh Day partner Sarah Moore, who heads up the firm's investigations into PFAS pollution, revealed that they are looking into the possibility of legal action on behalf of residents in Thornton-Cleveleys. She said: "So far, around 60 residents have contacted us about a range of issues, including possible health impacts and the potential reduction of property value."

News.title: Nostalgic 90s high street giant closes final stand-alone shops this month
News.content:
Nostalgic 90s high street giant closes final stand-alone shops this month

Popular retailer GAME has closed its last three shops after the company slowly scaled back - but fans don't need to worry as it's not closing for good

View 2 Images It's another blow to the UK high street as the popular retailer has closed its final standalone shops (Image: Mike Kemp/In Pictures via Getty Images)

It's the end of an era for 90s kids as high street giant GAME pulls the shutters on its final remaining stand-alone store.

‌



Popular in the 90s and 2000's GAME used to be the go-to for the latest games, consoles and accessories for all ages.

‌



Closures in Lancaster and the Merry Hill shopping centre and Sutton Coldfield mean that the iconic purple fronted shops that defined a generation no longer exist.

‌



But fans of the shop don't need to worry, as they can still purchase games online, and there will be around 200 concessions in Sports Direct and House of Fraser.

NatWest closing 37 branches with 34 confirmed for 2026 and 2027 - full list READ MORE :

View 2 Images Three final stores have closed (Image: Getty)

This comes after the business entered administration earlier this year and scaled down its operations, indicating it was unable to pay its debts.

‌



Ex-managing director Nick Arran had previously said the company will be the "last man standing" when it comes to selling physical games.

Speaking with GamesIndustry.biz in 2023, he hit back at claims they'd moved away from focusing on games, telling the site: "Gaming is our core business and we will be last man standing selling physical video games.

"We see our place in the market as proving that there is a place for physical, whether that be the collector's editions, which we see as the vinyl of video games, or the gifter who doesn't want to wrap up a download code for Christmas. But we need to be realistic. We have a business to run and the expectation is this will decline. So we need to fill that gap."

‌



Game emerged onto the high street in 1992 and quickly became the place to go for those purchasing video games, accessories and consoles. This led it to earn the reputation as the go-to for new releases, trade-ins and deals in store.

But it found itself in challenging times due to the increasing number of consumers opting for digital downloads to access new games, which is a stark contrast to when the store first launched in 1990.

Likely due to the surge in online shopping, another British high street retailer is also becoming a less common sight. Fashion chain River Island shut 27 stores at the start of this year throughout the UK. Despite the brand launching its first store in 1988 and becoming a familiar name across the country, its presence is now dwindling. Locations lost include Leeds Birstall Park, Surrey Quays in London, and Poole.

Article continues below

This is similar to fashion retailer QUIZ, originally established in Scotland back in 1993, faces potential store closures after entering administration in February 2026. Additionally, Claire's Accessories, which launched its first UK outlet in 1996, has entered administration. The chain is currently seeking a buyer. Should the business fail to attract a purchaser, then as many as 150 UK branches could be forced to shut their doors.

News.title: British boy, 9, stuck abroad after distraught family told he can't return home with them
News.content:
British boy, 9, stuck abroad after distraught family told he can't return home with them

A nine-year-old boy from Cardiff is stuck in Romania after UK border control denied him boarding at Milan airport despite being born in Wales

View 3 Images David was born in Cardiff and has lived in Wales for his entire life (Image: Chris Baker)

A nine-year-old boy from Cardiff is stuck abroad after his distraught family were told he was not able to return home to the UK after a routine family trip.

‌



David Toropu and his mum are now stranded in Romania waiting to find out when they might be able to return home following a recent UK government rule change.

‌



David, his mum Christina, and her husband and stepson had been on a rugby tour to Venice in the first week of the Easter holidays. After a four-night stay the family then arrived to check in at Milan airport on Thursday (April 2) for their return flight to London Gatwick.

‌



They expected to travel smoothly through all the airport checks, as they had done on the way out, but were met with an unexpected problem - they were told David could not board a flight to the UK as the UK border control held no record of his UK residency.

View 3 Images David and his family had been in Venice for a rugby tour (Image: Chris Baker)

Italy airport strikes update as three UK tourist hotspots face disruption - key dates READ MORE :

Despite being born in Cardiff and spending his entire life in Wales, David holds a Romanian passport, with his parents having relocated to the UK a year before his birth. His mum explained that both she and David's father are Romanian nationals and that her husband holds settled status while she has pre-settled status.

‌



Christina said: "I wasn't aware that I needed to apply for his own status because since he was born in 2016 after seven years of continuous residency he was supposed to get automatic British citizenship.

"Because I thought that was given automatically to him he wouldn't need to have his own settled or pre-settled status since he would have dual citizenship. However, the rules have changed since Brexit and I wasn't aware of that.", reports Wales Online.

With her son unable to return home, Christina had to stay in Italy with him while her stepson and husband returned to the UK to allow him to go to school and her husband to return to work. The mum and son spent two further nights in Italy before travelling to Romania, where they are staying with family until David is able to travel home.

‌



Christina said: "The UK border said they didn't hold any record of David ever being in the UK but he goes to school, he's enrolled in many public things like football, his GP is in the UK, his whole life is over there. He's only left the UK once when he was two years old for two weeks.

"Since he was denied I've had multiple panic attacks, I'm losing my head and I can't stop crying. He's used to his routines, his comfort in his house and everything that is his normal life. He heard the whole conversation of him being refused at the border and he was asking what was going to happen to him. In his mind he was thinking they were going to take me back to the UK and leave him in Italy."

At the airport, Christina tried to rectify the situation by applying for an electronic travel authorisation (ETA) but because the visa is intended for travel to the UK rather than residency and his registered address is in the UK, immigration officials insisted he was unable to return.

‌



View 3 Images 'I'm really concerned to hear about David's situation, and I've been in contact with his family to offer support,' said Alex Davies-Jones, David's constituency MP (Image: Chris Baker)

Christina is now worried that resolving the situation could result in David missing substantial amounts of school and her missing vital health appointments in the UK. She is also concerned about the substantial costs she has faced as a result of the mix-up, having spent around £2,000 on hotel rooms, flights and applications in less than a week.

She said: "We have made a really big dent into our savings and the rugby team my stepson plays for has created a gofundme to try and help us with the costs. In the Italian hotel we had the cheapest and smallest room and it cost £157 a night by itself."

‌



David's constituency MP, Alex Davies-Jones, told Wales Online: "I'm really concerned to hear about David's situation, and I've been in contact with his family to offer support. This is clearly a very distressing experience for both David and his mum.

"My office is doing everything we can to assist the family in resolving this as quickly as possible, and I will continue to support them in any way I can to help bring David home safely."

In February, the UK government rolled out a new travel system changing the rules for many visitors and dual nationals entering the UK. The system means dual nationals are required to either show a British passport or a new digital version of the certificate of entitlement to the right of abode or they risk being denied entry.

Article continues below

Dual nationals used to be able to travel to the UK without such a certificate using their non-British passport. Certificates of entitlement are not automatically issued meaning some people have spent decades living in the UK and have never needed to apply for them before.

The government is therefore urging dual nationals to apply for either a British passport, which costs around £100 for an adult, or a certificate of entitlement, which carries a fee of £589.

A spokesperson from the Home Office said the necessary documentation has now been granted.

News.title: Liverpool refuse to wave white flag, but don’t bet on another famous comeback
News.content:
Van Dijk, who has won eight major trophies during his eight years with Liverpool, said that the team had let down both their manager and the fans, before pointedly adding: “But also you shouldn’t give up, and that’s maybe what happened at a certain point.”

Upon arriving at the Parc des Princes for their Champions League quarter-final first leg against defending Paris St Germian, Wirtz was also asked if the players still had faith in Slot, whose position has come under enormous scrutiny following Saturday’s defeat. With the gap to Arsenal in the Premier League now 21 points, the Champions League is Liverpool’s last remaining hope of a trophy this season.

Asked if they were still playing for the manager, Wirtz said: “Yes of course we are believing in the manager. The team should believe in the manager because they won the league last season. We have a lot of good games this season.”

Slot himself was more nuanced in responding to Van Dijk’s comments, claiming that Liverpool had actually played well in going toe-to-toe with Manchester City for the opening 35 minutes. “Usually in football moments that hurt you most are just before half time and just after half time,” said Slot of City’s burst of goals between the 39th and 57th minute.

“[At 3-0] I saw indeed five minutes in between where it was too open and players were struggling. After the 4-0, City seemed to be OK with the 4-0. We had the ball. Not able to create that much any more. I didn’t see players giving up in the part of the game

“But I think it’s also good from a captain that he has a strong and firm reaction after a game like that. Hopefully it’s not only immediately after a game and we can as a team show a strong and firm reaction.

“[It was] the only four chances we gave away in the game by the way. The good thing is that during this year we have become quite experienced in terms of negativity because of all the setbacks we have had this season.”

News.title: Droughts driving spread of drug-resistant infections, research shows
News.content:
Droughts are driving the spread of antibiotic resistant infections around the world, research has shown.

Researchers from the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) analysed samples taken from around the globe and found that the more arid the soil, the greater the concentration of antibiotic resistant bacteria it contained.

Their findings, published in Nature Microbiology late last month, show that a natural selection process is effectively supercharged when soil dries up.

Naturally occurring antibiotics produced by microorganisms in the soil become more concentrated during a drought, creating conditions that favour resistant strains, they write.

Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) occurs when microbes evolve to resist the drugs used to treat infections. Drug-resistant infections already kill a million people every year and could cause 10 million deaths a year by the middle of this century, according to the United Nations.

For decades, much of the effort on tackling AMR has focused on curbing the overuse of antibiotics in healthcare, but the Caltech research suggests that natural processes could also be fuelling the phenomenon.

“Droughts are creating the same effects as overuse of antibiotics in the clinic: They both drive selection for antibiotics resistance,” said Dianne Newman, a Professor of Biology and Geobiology at Caltech and a co-author of the study.

The researchers also compared clinical surveillance data from 116 countries with data on soil conditions and identified a strong correlation between the frequency of antibiotic resistance and aridity.

“We’re interacting with soil all the time, whether it’s recreational or simply by inhaling dust,” said Xiaoyu Shan, a Caltech postdoctoral scholar who led the study.

“Importantly, bacteria are able to transfer genes to each other, and antibiotic-resistance genes are known to have a high rate of transfer. With trillions of bacteria in the environment, this is a substantial occurrence.”

Sports.title: Atletico Madrid almost concede bizarre penalty in Arsenal-like blunder as Barcelona boss fumes at VAR
Sports.content:
ATLETICO MADRID almost conceded a penalty after a controversial gaffe against Barcelona in the Champions League.

Atletico picked up a massive 2-0 victory over Barca in Wednesday’s first leg of their quarter-final at the Nou Camp.





But the Catalan outfit were left incensed as they claimed they should have been awarded a spot-kick in the 55th minute.

Atleti led 1-0 after Julian Alvarez’s opener while the hosts were down to 10 men following Pau Cubarsi’s straight red card.

Atletico took on a goal-kick and controversy ensued as keeper Juan Musso passed the ball to team-mate Marc Pubill inside the box.

Pubill then caught the ball with his hand and placed it on the goal line before passing it back to Musso.

Believing the ball was in play, Barcelona were infuriated and demanded a penalty as well as a red card for the centre-back, who was on a yellow.

Tensions rose after Atletico scored a second with Alexander Sorloth on 70 minutes to give the visitors a massive advantage ahead of next Tuesday’s return fixture at the Wanda Metropolitano Stadium.

There is an argument to be made that common sense dictates there was no pressure and no advantage to be gained.

And there is a precedent as Arsenal star Gabriel Magalhaes did the same thing in the Champions League two years ago during a 2-2 draw in the quarter-finals.

The Gunners were awarded a goal-kick and keeper David Raya passed the ball to Gabriel, who picked it up, placed it back down and switched it back to his team-mate.

But Barcelona boss Hansi Flick would have none of it as he insisted his team should have been awarded a pen.

Flick told CBS Sports: “I think they deserved the red card. The goalkeeper plays the ball, it’s clear play and he stops it with the hand.

“It’s a double yellow and it’s a red card and a penalty normally for me.”

Sports.title: ‘You’ve got to commend him’ – Mo Salah hailed for what he did after Liverpool lost to PSG despite brutal snub

MOHAMED SALAH has been hailed for his professionalism despite being snubbed against Paris Saint-Germain.

The Egyptian star was left on the bench by manager Arne Slot as Liverpool were beaten 2-0 in France.





The Reds were left with a mountain to climb if they are to progress to the Champions League semi-finals.

Salah, 33, had to watch on as his team-mates were outdone by goals from Desire Doué and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Liverpool failed to have a single shot on target during the game.

But despite not being on the pitch, he was able to impress the likes of former stars Stuart Pearce and Steven Gerrard.

Speaking on talkSPORT, he said: “I’m also watching down here Mo Salah doing his running as well.

“So you’ve got to commend him for that. I know it’s his job. I understand that.”

The Reds rolled the dice in a bid to combat PSG's threats on Wednesday night, but were ultimately undone in Paris. They were outclassed and were arguably lucky to only lose 2-0 given the dominance of the French champions.

‌



Slot named Virgil van Dijk, Ibrahima Konate and Joe Gomez in his backline with Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong making it a back five out of possession. It didn't stop the European champions dominating the evening as they scored in either half.

‌



Enrique is eyeing a third Champions League title as a manager and knows that opposition are always prone to a new innovation against them, so was not put off by Liverpool's experiment, which did little to halt the Paris juggernaut.

The Spanish boss told Canal Plus: "It’s a surprise because it’s the first time Arne Slot has played with three at the back this year. It showed that they’re changing and trying something new, which is normal. We’re used to opponents adapting to us, so no worries. We’ll be looking to win the second game."

Enrique went on to tell TNT Sports: "I know Arne Slot is a great coach, it’s the first time they play with five at the back. But we are used to seeing other teams change formation to play against us, it’s normal.

‌



"I think they played a great match, they are a physical team, very strong, have individual, quality players and it was a very nice match. It’s always a pleasure playing against Arne Slot and his teams because they try to play football in an offensive play and it was nice to watch."

View 2 Images Liverpool had hoped to try and contain the likes of Achraf Hakimi with their formation tweak

Slot himself is a man under pressure with the Champions League presenting the club's last chance for silverware this term. They were always up against it given PSG's form and will now have to try and overturn a two-goal deficit back at Anfield next week.

‌



The Liverpool boss admitted that his thought process centre around trying to contain PSG duo Achraf Hakimi and Nuno Mendes, who have long been huge threats out on the wings.

He said: "They have pace from everywhere all over the pitch, so it doesn’t matter where you look, you see pace, incredible pace, Hakimi and Nuno Mendes are an unbelievable offensive threat, apart from all the others, so we played with Jeremie Frimpong and Milos Kerkez, that was the thought behind it."

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher brutally claims Liverpool played like a 'lower division team' in PSG loss
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher brutally claims Liverpool played like a 'lower division team' in PSG loss

Liverpool were well beaten by PSG in their Champions League clash with the performance levels proving alarming as Jamie Carragher commented on how it didn't look like two top flight teams squaring off

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher was alarmed by the gap between the two teams (Image: CBS Sports Golazo/YouTube)

Jamie Carragher confessed that seeing Liverpool lose to PSG was "like watching a team from a lower division" such was the gulf in class on Wednesday night.

‌



The Reds left the Parc des Princes having lost the first leg 2-0, but the manner of the performance suggests it could've been far more damaging. PSG scored in either half, first through Desire Doue and then Khvicha Kvaratskhelia finished impressively to double their lead.

‌



Liverpool were always heading into the tie as underdogs given their struggles this season and PSG's tag as European champions, but the gap between the two teams alarmed Carragher, who couldn't believe the difference from 12 months ago when the two teams played out a hugely competitive knockout tie.

‌



Arne Slot's side have fallen off a cliff since then and European success in their only remaining trophy hope, but that looks to all but have gone despite a return leg to come.

Carragher said on CBS Sports: "That was like watching a team from a lower division. The gulf in class was very worrying from a Liverpool point of view. In some ways, it's a great result as it should have been five or six. But the gulf between the two teams was absolutely startling when you consider last season.

Liverpool star singled out by Steven Gerrard after 'cruel' PSG goal READ MORE :

"Yes, Liverpool got battered at PSG and they won 1-0, we know that. But the second leg at Anfield was a really close game, two top teams. Liverpool then go and spend £450m, probably a lot more than PSG spent in the summer. To see the gulf there is worrying. You think, how's it got to that? How's it got that bad?"

‌



Liverpool changed tactics and began with a back five, which is not common practice for this team. The tweak failed to have the desired affect as PSG were just as dominant and Carragher felt "they were actually more open with the back five than they would be with the back four".

View 2 Images Liverpool's tactical tweak failed to have the desired affect (Image: Justin Setterfield, Getty Images)

Despite the gulf in class the tie does remain open, albeit PSG will be huge favourites to get the job done even if they do have to go to Anfield. The demise at Liverpool has been such that the likes of PSV have come to Merseyside and won this season, but Slot remained defiant.

Article continues below

He said: "We're lucky to only lose 2-0 as they had more chances than they scored, although the first goal felt harsh as we didn't give anything away. It's very good we're still in the tie. We can bring them to Anfield with how much a difference Anfield can make for us."

Sports.title: 'I'm Man Utd legend but the year after leaving the club was the best of my life'
Sports.content:
'I'm Man Utd legend but the year after leaving the club was the best of my life'

The former Manchester United man has lifted the lid on his life since leaving Old Trafford

View 3 Images David de Gea spent 12 seasons at United (Image: Matt McNulty, Getty Images)

Former Manchester United goalkeeper David de Gea has spoken candidly about his year away from football. The Spaniard has described those 12 months as the "best" of his life.

‌



De Gea became an icon at Old Trafford. The now 35-year-old secured the Premier League, FA Cup and League Cup under Sir Alex Ferguson as he established himself as one of the finest shot-stoppers in the world.

‌



Following 12 seasons at United, he departed in July 2023 and spent the whole of the 2023/24 campaign as a free agent before putting pen to paper with Serie A outfit Fiorentina, where he remains to this day. Thursday will see De Gea return to England with La Viola as they face Crystal Palace in the first leg of the Europa Conference League quarter-finals.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The former Atletico Madrid stalwart has experienced a patchy season in Florence, with Paolo Vanoli's side finding themselves dragged into a relegation battle. De Gea and his colleagues have since engineered a remarkable turnaround, though, and started ascending the Serie A table.

Reflecting on his time spent away from the sport after leaving United, De Gea told Gazetta: "It was an easy decision. After 12 years at United, I needed a break.

‌



Man Utd confirm two injury boosts as four youngsters named in training camp squad READ MORE :

"So I took a year off to dedicate to my family and friends: it was the best year of my life. But I continued to train with a coach, Craig, who was very supportive and did a great job with me.

"I was sure I could compete at a high level again. When Fiorentina called me, I was ready. The first time I walked into Rocco B. Commisso Viola Park, I was speechless: there aren't many facilities like it in Europe."

View 3 Images De Gea was a free agent for a season before Fiorentina took a chance on him (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Watch Crystal Palace vs Fiorentina on TNT Sports This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £30.99 TNT Sports Get TNT Sports here Product Description Crystal Palace have reached the UEFA Conference League quarter-finals where they host Fiorentina on April 9. Fans can watch the game on TNT Sports via HBO Max or Prime Video's TNT Sports channel.

De Gea spoke enthusiastically about his years in Manchester. He described Sir Alex as a "father figure" and said the heartbreaking Premier League defeat to local rivals Manchester City in 2012 proved the catalyst for United's title triumph the following campaign.

"We lost the Premier League in our first year when City took the title from us with a last-minute win despite our victory over Sunderland. I made up for it by winning it in 2012/13 - every game at United was special," he continued.

‌



Discussing Fiorentina's struggles this term, he said: "There's no explanation. We started badly and put a lot of pressure on ourselves. It was tough for me too, as I found myself fighting for survival for the first time.

View 3 Images De Gea will return to England to face Crystal Palace (Image: Getty Images)

"The young players suffered more; in these situations, you have to be mentally strong. I wasn't at my best either, but I didn't give up. Hard work is the only way to get out of it.

Article continues below

"The hardest moment was at the end of 2025, when we were last, hadn't won a game, and the statistics said no one in our situation had ever survived. I was worried then: I felt like I was in a nightmare. Now, however, we've improved in many areas and are still in the running in the Conference, but we have to keep working hard."

The clash with Palace has captured the star's attention, with a return to England always an enticing proposition. He concluded: "We're focused on Serie A, but we have to believe in it. Crystal Palace are strong, and it'll be great for me to return to England. Winning a trophy would be amazing for the fans; we can do it."
